relations.subject: n1ql:alter-index
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate. NOTE: the 7.2 record MINTED a separate predicate `wholeStatementRequiresEdition` here, arguing that requiresEdition was defined only for a clause/option rather than a whole statement. I am reusing requiresEdition, because (a) wholeStatementRequiresEdition was never promoted, (b) the registry's requiresEdition has no documented arity restriction to clauses, and (c) maintaining two predicates that differ only in subject granularity is exactly the kind of split reconciliation should avoid. relations.evidence: This statement is applicable only for Standard GSI (Plasma) and MOI Indexes; and hence supported only for Couchbase Server Enterprise Edition nodes. (Not applicable for Forest DB.)

relations.subject: n1ql:alter-index
relations.evidence: Altering indexes is only supported in Couchbase Server 5.5 and later; if any nodes in the cluster are running a version of Couchbase Server earlier than 5.5, then this statement will not work.

relations.subject: n1ql:alter-index-replica-management
relations.evidence: In addition, altering the number of replicas or deleting an index replica is only supported in Couchbase Server 6.5 and later; if any nodes in the cluster are running a version of Couchbase Server earlier than 6.5, then these operations will not work.

notable_absence.finding: This is the only index statement in the batch that gates on a coarse RBAC ROLE (Administrator) rather than a fine-grained privilege. CREATE INDEX and CREATE VECTOR INDEX both name privilege:query-manage-index; ALTER INDEX names no privilege at all, only the Administrator role. That asymmetry is stable across 7.2 and 8.0, so it is a real access-model fact rather than a docs omission: index placement is treated as a cluster-administration operation, not a keyspace-scoped query operation. Worth asserting in the ontology that requiresRole and requiresPrivilege are not interchangeable and that this page is the canonical example.

cross_component_finding: The page's edition gate is expressed via index STORAGE technologies (Standard GSI/Plasma, MOI, Forest DB) which have no home in the current registry - storage-engine: covers only couchstore and magma, i.e. the Data service. Reconciliation needs either an index-storage-engine: namespace or an explicit note that storage-engine: is data-service-only. Do not merge index-type:forestdb with anything in storage-engine:; ForestDB was an index storage format, and a same-name collision with the data-service engines would be a genuine modelling error.
cross_product_finding: Sharp, well-evidenced divergence on the same clause. Server 8.0 says the nodes property is unavailable CONDITIONALLY, on an opt-in cluster setting: 'You cannot use this property if you have enabled file-based index rebalancing.' The Capella twin says both the nodes property and action:move are unavailable UNCONDITIONALLY, because of a platform default: 'You cannot use this property in Couchbase Capella, as it defaults to file-based index rebalancing' and 'You cannot use this statement to move indexes or index replicas in Couchbase Capella, as it defaults to file-based index rebalancing.' So the Capella record's `n1ql:alter-index-with-nodes behavesDifferentlyUnder deployment:capella` and the Server relation `indexes:file-based-index-rebalancing disablesFeatureFor n1ql:alter-index-with-nodes` are the SAME underlying mechanism at two levels of abstraction - Capella's restriction is a consequence of a setting Capella happens to default to, not a separate Capella-specific rule. Reconciliation can now collapse the Capella deployment:capella facts into (deployment:capella hasDefaultSetting indexes:file-based-index-rebalancing) + the Server-side disablesFeatureFor relation, which is strictly more informative than either record alone. This is the strongest argument in this batch that the registry needs a settings axis rather than treating Capella-vs-Server as primitive. Two further divergences: (1) Server gates the whole statement on edition:enterprise; the Capella page has no edition sentence at all (Capella has no editions), so requiresEdition facts are structurally Server-only. (2) Server names role:administrator; Capella names Basic->Write / Advanced->Query Index. Do not merge.
version_finding: SAME-PAGE 7.2-vs-8.0 COMPARISON. THREE 7.2 version gates have been silently removed at 8.0, and one 7.2-derived relation no longer holds. (a) 7.2: 'In Couchbase Server 7.0 and later, you can use the index name with the ON keyword and a keyspace reference to specify the keyspace on which the index is built.' 8.0 drops the qualifier: 'You can use the index name with the ON keyword and a keyspace reference to specify the keyspace on which the index is built.' The 7.2 relation `n1ql:alter-index-keyspace-on-syntax availableSince version:server-7.0` therefore has NO evidence at 8.0. It remains historically true but is unrecoverable from the 8.0 tree. (b) 7.2: 'In Couchbase Server 6.5 and later, the index type for a secondary index must be Global Secondary Index (GSI).' 8.0 drops the qualifier. The 7.2 relation `n1ql:alter-index availableSince version:server-6.5` (the record's second, USING-clause-scoped assertion) therefore also loses its evidence at 8.0 - and note it was a dubious assertion anyway, since it attached a whole-statement availableSince to a fact about the USING clause. (c) 7.2: 'In Couchbase Server 7.0 and later, the index redistribution setting enables you to specify how Couchbase Server redistributes indexes automatically on rebalance.' 8.0 drops the qualifier. The 7.2 record used that sentence as evidence for a seeAlso to learn:rebalance, so the seeAlso survives but its version content does not. (d) The two version gates that DID survive verbatim-in-substance are 5.5 (whole statement) and 6.5 (replica management), both rephrased from 'if the cluster is a mix of Couchbase Server 5.5 and previous versions' to 'if any nodes in the cluster are running a version of Couchbase Server earlier than 5.5' - the same fact, better English. NEW AT 8.0: the ALTER VECTOR INDEX synonym sentence, and the file-based-index-rebalancing restriction on the nodes property. Also new: 7.2 called this construct a 'directive' ('run the ALTER INDEX directive'), 8.0 consistently calls it a 'statement' - a terminology normalisation that will break any naive string matching between the two trees. CONCLUSION FOR THE WAVE: the dominant version-drift pattern in Couchbase's SQL++ reference is gate ATTRITION, not deprecation. Old 'in version X and later' qualifiers are deleted once X is far enough behind the current release, so an extraction run only against server/current systematically under-counts availableSince facts, and the ontology's version coverage will silently DEGRADE with each release unless older trees are extracted too or the facts are pinned once discovered.
